title: Creation and the Fall, part 3 of 3: The Fall
style: Classical oil painting on canvas, visible expressive brushstrokes and palette-knife texture, dramatic chiaroscuro, rich earthy palette of ochre, umber, olive and deep blue. The primeval world at its beginning: untouched wilderness, no buildings, no tools, no metal, no woven cloth, nothing man-made beyond what the scene describes. Cinematic 16:9 landscape composition. No text, no borders, no watermark, no modern objects.

blocks.GARDEN: the Garden of Eden, a lush sunlit garden of fruit trees of many kinds, flowering shrubs, ferns and clear streams, with no walls, no paths, no buildings and nothing man-made
blocks.TREE_LIFE: the tree of life, a tall radiant tree with smooth silver-white bark, bright green leaves and softly glowing golden fruit
blocks.TREE_KNOW: the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, a broad ancient tree with a dark twisted trunk, deep green glossy leaves and clusters of round crimson-and-gold fruit unlike the fruit of any other tree
blocks.SERPENT: the serpent, a large and beautiful snake with iridescent bronze-green scales and bright, watchful amber eyes, its long body wound around a branch of the tree with its head lifted high. It is an ordinary snake in shape: no arms, no legs, no wings, no horns and no human features
blocks.SERPENT_DUST: the serpent, a large snake with bronze-green scales and amber eyes, down on the bare ground, crawling flat on its belly through dry dust. It is an ordinary snake in shape: no arms, no legs, no wings and no human features
blocks.PRESENCE: a moving radiance of golden-white light that passes between the tree trunks like sunlight walking through the garden, the leaves and grass stirring in a breeze around it; the light has no figure, no face and no human shape
blocks.OUTSIDE: the land outside the garden: dry stony ground with sparse brown grass, thorn bushes and thistles under a dusky sky, with no buildings, no paths and nothing man-made
blocks.CHERUBIM: cherubim, towering winged heavenly guardians many times the height of a man, with great outspread wings of gold and fire, their bodies so bright that no face can be made out; awe-inspiring, not infants and not cupids
blocks.SWORD: a whirling sword of flame, a single blazing sword turning by itself in the air, held in no hand, throwing off rings of fire
blocks.ONE: Exactly one person in the picture, no one else
blocks.NOLIGHTFIG: No figure, no face and no human shape in the light

segs.text: Now the serpent was more crafty than any beast of the field that the LORD God had made.
And he said to the woman,
Did God really say, ‘You must not eat from any tree in the garden?’
The woman answered the serpent,
We may eat the fruit of the trees of the garden, but about the fruit of the tree in the middle of the garden, God has said, ‘You must not eat of it or touch it, or you will die.’
You will not surely die,
the serpent told the woman.
For God knows that in the day you eat of it, your eyes will be opened and you will be like God, knowing good and evil.
When the woman saw that the tree was good for food and pleasing to the eyes, and that it was desirable for obtaining wisdom, she took the fruit and ate it.
She also gave some to her husband who was with her, and he ate it.
And the eyes of both of them were opened, and they knew that they were naked; so they sewed together fig leaves and made coverings for themselves.
Then the man and his wife heard the voice of the LORD God walking in the garden in the breeze of the day, and they hid themselves from the presence of the LORD God among the trees of the garden.
But the LORD God called out to the man,
Where are you?
I heard Your voice in the garden,
he replied,
and I was afraid because I was naked; so I hid myself.
Who told you that you were naked?
asked the LORD God.
Have you eaten from the tree of which I commanded you not to eat?
And the man answered,
The woman whom You gave me, she gave me fruit from the tree, and I ate it.
Then the LORD God said to the woman,
What is this you have done?
The serpent deceived me,
she replied,
and I ate.
So the LORD God said to the serpent:
Because you have done this, cursed are you above all livestock and every beast of the field! On your belly will you go, and dust you will eat, all the days of your life.
And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her seed. He will crush your head, and you will strike his heel.
To the woman He said:
I will sharply increase your pain in childbirth; in pain you will bring forth children. Your desire will be for your husband, and he will rule over you.
And to Adam He said:

Because you have listened to the voice of your wife and have eaten from the tree of which I commanded you not to eat, cursed is the ground because of you; through toil you will eat of it all the days of your life.
Both thorns and thistles it will yield for you, and you will eat the plants of the field.
By the sweat of your brow you will eat your bread, until you return to the ground— because out of it were you taken. For dust you are, and to dust you shall return.
And Adam named his wife Eve, because she would be the mother of all the living.
And the LORD God made garments of skin for Adam and his wife, and He clothed them.
Then the LORD God said,
Behold, the man has become like one of Us, knowing good and evil. And now, lest he reach out his hand and take also from the tree of life, and eat, and live forever...
Therefore the LORD God banished him from the Garden of Eden to work the ground from which he had been taken.
So He drove out the man and stationed cherubim on the east side of the Garden of Eden, along with a whirling sword of flame to guard the way to the tree of life.

The breeze of the day in {GARDEN}: late afternoon, a wind moving through the tree tops, and far off among the trunks {PRESENCE}. {NOPEOPLE}. {NOLIGHTFIG}. Wide view.

{ADAM_FIG}, and {EVE_FIG}, running away through the undergrowth of the garden, seen from behind, pushing branches aside, a golden light growing among the trees far behind the viewer and throwing their shadows ahead of them. {TWO}. Wide view from behind.

Close view of {ADAM_FIG}, hiding in shadow behind a tree trunk with his back pressed to the bark, eyes shut tight and jaw clenched as golden light edges around the trunk and touches his shoulder. Head and shoulders only. {ONE}.

{ADAM_FIG}, stepping out half-way from behind a tree trunk into strong golden-white light, one hand raised to shield his eyes, his head lowered, answering. {ONE}. {NOLIGHTFIG}. Medium view, full figure, the light coming from out of frame on the right.

{EVE_FIG}, on the left, speaking and pointing with one outstretched arm at a large bronze-green snake coiled on the lowest branch of the dark tree on the right. The snake has no limbs and no human features. {ONE}. Medium view.

A wide dry field of cracked earth under a hard white sky, a few thin stalks of wild grain growing among stones, and far away one small figure of a man bent over the ground, working. Exactly one tiny distant figure. No buildings, no tools, no animals. Very wide view.

Thorns and thistles: close view of spiny thistles and long hooked thorn branches thrusting up out of cracked dry soil, crowding around a few thin stalks of wild grain. {NOPEOPLE}. Close view at ground level.

By the sweat of your brow: extreme close view of a brown-skinned man's forehead and brow under dark curly hair, beaded with sweat and streaked with dust under a harsh sun. Only the brow, eyes and hair fill the frame.
Out of the ground you were taken: {ADAM_FIG}, kneeling on bare earth and looking down at a handful of dry dust that he has scooped up in his cupped hands. {ONE}. Medium view.

For dust you are, and to dust you shall return: close view of a man's open brown hand with dry dust pouring out between the fingers and blowing away on the wind against a low golden light. Only the hand and the dust are in the frame; no face and no body. Close framing.

Adam names his wife Eve: {ADAM_FIG}, on the left, turning to {EVE_FIG}, on the right, and taking her hand in both of his, speaking her name to her with a grave, gentle face. {TWO}. Medium view from the side.
The mother of all the living: close portrait of {EVE_FIG}, lifting her eyes with the first trace of hope on her tear-marked face, soft evening light on her. Head and shoulders only. {ONE}.

The LORD God clothes them: {ADAM_SKIN}, on the left, and {EVE_SKIN}, on the right, kneeling side by side with bowed heads under {GLORY} that rests gently on their shoulders. {TWO}. Medium-wide view from the front.

Garments of skin: close view of a young woman's brown hands tying a strip of hide at the waist of a simple garment of tawny brown animal skin that she is wearing, while a wilted covering of sewn fig leaves lies discarded on the ground at her feet. Only her hands, waist and the garment are in the frame; no face. Close framing.

{ADAM_SKIN}, on the left, and {EVE_SKIN}, on the right, standing together clothed at the edge of a garden glade in evening light, he drawing the skin garment straight on her shoulder with care. {TWO}. Medium view, full figures.
The LORD God speaks: {GLORY}, standing high over the whole garden at dusk, the tree tops dark below it. {NOPEOPLE}. Very wide view.
{TREE_LIFE}, standing in the middle of the garden at dusk, shining in the gathering dark, its golden fruit within easy reach of the ground. {NOPEOPLE}. No snake. Medium view from below.

In the left foreground {ADAM_SKIN}, seen from the side, looking across a dark glade at {TREE_LIFE}, which stands shining at a distance on the right. His hands are at his sides and he holds nothing. {ONE}. Wide view.

A wall of golden-white light rising between the viewer and a shining tree with silver-white bark and golden fruit, so that the tree is seen only dimly through the brightness. {NOLIGHTFIG}. {NOPEOPLE}. Medium view.

Banished from the Garden of Eden: {ADAM_SKIN}, and {EVE_SKIN}, walking away side by side between the last trees of the garden toward open barren country, seen from behind, the green garden glowing with light behind the viewer and their long shadows stretching ahead. {TWO}. Wide view from behind.

The edge of the garden: close view of a man's and a woman's bare feet stepping off the last green grass onto dry, stony, dusty ground. Only the feet, ankles and the hems of tawny skin garments are in the frame; no faces. Close view at ground level.
To work the ground from which he had been taken: {ADAM_SKIN}, on his knees in {OUTSIDE}, breaking the hard soil with a stout broken branch held in both hands. {ONE}. No metal tools. Medium view.

He drives out the man: {ADAM_SKIN}, and {EVE_SKIN}, hurrying down a stony slope toward the viewer with a great wind and a blaze of golden-white light at their backs, he with an arm around her shoulders, both looking back over their shoulders. {TWO}. {NOLIGHTFIG}. Medium-wide view from the front.

On the east side of the Garden of Eden: two {CHERUBIM}, stationed side by side before the dark wall of the garden's trees at nightfall, and between them {SWORD}. {NOPEOPLE}. Wide low view looking up at them.
Close view of {SWORD}, against the night-dark trees of the garden, sparks streaming from it in every direction. {NOPEOPLE}. No hand holds it.

The way to the tree of life is guarded: far beyond a turning blaze of fire and the bright wings of towering guardians, a tall tree with silver-white bark and softly glowing golden fruit stands deep inside the dark garden, out of reach. No faces can be made out in the brightness. {NOPEOPLE}. Wide view looking into the garden from outside.
Close view of {EVE_SKIN}, outside the garden at night, looking back over her shoulder, firelight flickering red and gold on her face and tears on her cheek. Head and shoulders only. {ONE}.

Night in {OUTSIDE}. Two tiny figures, a man and a woman in garments of skin, walk away across the empty land in the foreground, seen from behind; far behind them on the horizon the dark line of the garden is lit by winged fire and a turning flame. Exactly two people, tiny in the landscape. Very wide view.

card_notes: Every spoken word is Scripture: Genesis 3:1–24, complete.
notes: Text: Genesis 3:1-24 in full, no verses skipped or abridged. Speakers: N narrator, S the serpent, E the woman (Eve), A the man (Adam), G the voice of God. v22 ends with the ellipsis the BSB itself prints.
Still tags: T = from the text, I = inferred, D = dramatized. REF = character reference sheet (not used in the film, no clip).

Faces: ADAM and EVE reuse refs/REF-ADAM.jpg and refs/REF-EVE.jpg and the description text from s01e01b unchanged. This unit adds two life stages, each derived from those portraits: fig-leaf coverings (v7 to v20: refs/REF-ADAM-FIG.jpg, refs/REF-EVE-FIG.jpg) and garments of skin (from v21: refs/REF-ADAM-SKIN.jpg, refs/REF-EVE-SKIN.jpg). Genesis 4 onward should start from the SKIN sheets.

Before v7 the pair are unclothed and unashamed; the body is hidden by hair, foliage and framing exactly as in s01e01b (HIDE_M, HIDE_F copied unchanged; PIPELINE default). The text does not say how large the fig-leaf coverings were: they are painted as a waist wrap for him and a collarbone-to-knee covering for her (I; the image service refuses anything scantier on a woman).
The two trees reuse TREE_KNOW and TREE_LIFE from s01e01b word for word. The fruit is of no named kind (not an apple): the text says only 'the fruit'.

The serpent: the text does not describe its form before the curse and the question is disputed, so nothing is resolved: it is an ordinary limbless snake throughout, kept up in the branches of the tree until v14 and shown on its belly in the dust only after the curse (N2 sliding down the trunk is I). Its voice is not explained.

v6 'her husband who was with her': Adam is first pictured at the giving of the fruit (F1), standing beside her under the tree. The dialogue stills (B-E) are framed on the woman and the serpent and neither show nor exclude him.

God is shown only as light, wind and voice: no figure, no face, no hands. 'Walking in the garden in the breeze of the day' (v8) is a radiance moving between the trunks with wind (PRESENCE). 'He clothed them' (v21) is light resting on the two already clothed; no animal is shown being killed. 'One of Us' (v22) is light only.
v15 is shown as the text says it and not interpreted: O1-O2 enmity between the woman and the serpent, O3 (D) a symbolic bare heel on the serpent's head with no identifiable person.

D: the judgements of v16-19 are spoken in the garden; Q3-Q5, R1-R2, S1 and S3 picture what the words describe (withering ground, toil, thorns, sweat, dust) as images under the voice, with hands, feet or a tiny distant figure only. P2 hands over her belly for v16; P3 for 'your desire will be for your husband'. C5 a withered leaf for 'or you will die' (echoes O6 in s01e01b). G2 the fallen fruit. L2, T2, X5 reactions.

v24: cherubim are plural and the sword is named separately from them ('along with a whirling sword of flame'), so two cherubim are shown and the sword turns by itself between them, held in no hand. Their appearance is I: towering, winged, too bright for any face to be seen (not infants). 'East side' is in the prompt but compass direction cannot be seen in the picture. X6 the pair walking into the land is D.
W3 and Q4 use a broken branch to work the ground: no made tools exist yet (I).
Voices for the serpent, Eve and Adam are placeholders chosen without hearing them (God and Adam as in s01e01a/b); narration is not generated in this unit.
